newsitem.title: USA: Pulte homebuilding revenues, profits rise.
newsitem.headline: Pulte homebuilding revenues, profits rise.

text.p: Pulte Corp said pre-tax profits from its homebuilding operations during the fourth quarter of 1996 increased three percent to $42.5 million from $41.1 million a year earlier, due largely to an increase in unit sales.
Pulte said its gross profit margins for the fourth quarter were flat with a year ago at 14.9 percent and down slightly from the 15.1 perceived in the third quarter of 1996.
Pulte said homebuilding revenues for the quarter increased primarily because of an 11 percent increase in housing units sold to 4,593 from 4,140 during the fourth quarter of 1995.
The homebuilding revenues for the fourth quarter of 1996 totaled $727.25 million, up 13 percent from the $641.7 million in the same period of 1995.
Unit net new orders increased two percent during the quarter to 3,161 units, or $515 million, from 3,089 units, or $488 million in the same quarter of 1995.
For the year ended December 31, 1996, unit net new orders were 14,443 units, or $2.32 billion, a four percent improvement from 13,868 units, or $2.16 billion, in 1995.
Housing unit backlog at December 31, 1996 was 3,469 units, or $598 million, compared with the 3,699 units, or $606 million, at December 31, 1995.
Pulte said it repurchased about 3.8 million shares of common stock in 1996, representing over 14 percent of the company's shares outstanding at the end of 1995.

Robert K. Burgess, President and Chief Executive Officer of Pulte Corp, said, "We are pleased with our 1996 achievements and we enter 1997 with an approach which continues to focus on improving our shareholder returns."

Pulte reported fourth quarter 1996 earnings from continuing operations of $25.3 million, or $1.08 per share, versus $23.5 million, or $0.86 a share, in the fourth quarter of 1995. For the full 1996 year, Pulte's earnings from continuing operations increased 29 percent to $63.2 million, or $2.52 per share, compared with $48.8 million, or $1.79 a share, in 1995.
